controls.label: Throttle
controls.info: 0 is disarmed. The numbers below are approx. for a 5-inch 6S quad on 2207 1750 KV motors.

layers.name: Bottom plate
layers.info: The lower plate of the frame body: the stack and the camera cage are bolted to it, the arms are clamped between it and the arm screws.

parts.name: Bottom plate
parts.info: 2 mm carbon fibre plate (approx.). Carbon is stiff and light, but it conducts: anything bare that touches it can short.

layers.name: Arms
layers.info: Four arms in a true X, 225 mm motor to motor across the diagonal (approx.).

parts.name: Arm 1
parts.info: 5 mm carbon arm (approx.). It carries the motor at its tip, and the motor wires run along its top.

parts.name: Arm 2
parts.info: 5 mm carbon arm (approx.). It carries the motor at its tip, and the motor wires run along its top.

parts.name: Arm 3
parts.info: 5 mm carbon arm (approx.). It carries the motor at its tip, and the motor wires run along its top.

parts.name: Arm 4
parts.info: 5 mm carbon arm (approx.). It carries the motor at its tip, and the motor wires run along its top.

parts.name: Standoffs
parts.info: Aluminium spacers that hold the top plate above the stack (approx. 32 mm).

parts.name: Receiver (ExpressLRS)
parts.info: Hears the pilot’s radio and passes the sticks to the flight controller over a serial line, in the CRSF protocol (approx.: a typical nano receiver).

parts.name: Receiver LED
parts.info: Solid: link up.

layers.name: Motors

parts.name: Motors
parts.info: Brushless outrunner. The stator and its windings stay still on the arm; the bell with its magnets turns around them.

parts.name: Bells (CW)
parts.info: The bell turns clockwise seen from above; diagonal motors turn the same way, so the four torques cancel and the quad does not spin.

parts.name: Prop shafts (CW)
parts.info: 5 mm shaft (M5 thread) the prop is clamped on.

parts.name: Bells (CCW)
parts.info: The bell turns anticlockwise seen from above; diagonal motors turn the same way, so the four torques cancel and the quad does not spin.

parts.name: Prop shafts (CCW)
parts.info: 5 mm shaft (M5 thread) the prop is clamped on.

layers.info: Motor 1 rear right, 2 front right, 3 rear left, 4 front left: Betaflight’s order. 1 and 4 turn clockwise, 2 and 3 anticlockwise.

layers.name: ESC

parts.name: ESC board
parts.info: Four motor drivers on one board. Each takes battery DC and makes three-phase AC for its motor, switching its six MOSFETs tens of thousands of times a second.

parts.name: Motor 1 MOSFETs
parts.info: Three half-bridges, one per phase of motor 1: two MOSFETs each, one to the battery +, one to −.

parts.name: M1 pads
parts.info: Where the three wires of motor 1 are soldered.

parts.name: Motor 2 MOSFETs
parts.info: Three half-bridges, one per phase of motor 2: two MOSFETs each, one to the battery +, one to −.

parts.name: M2 pads
parts.info: Where the three wires of motor 2 are soldered.

parts.name: Motor 3 MOSFETs
parts.info: Three half-bridges, one per phase of motor 3: two MOSFETs each, one to the battery +, one to −.

parts.name: M3 pads
parts.info: Where the three wires of motor 3 are soldered.

parts.name: Motor 4 MOSFETs
parts.info: Three half-bridges, one per phase of motor 4: two MOSFETs each, one to the battery +, one to −.

parts.name: M4 pads
parts.info: Where the three wires of motor 4 are soldered.

parts.name: ESC MCUs
parts.info: One small controller per motor reads the DShot commands and times the switching. SpeedyBee does not name the chip (labelled black box).

parts.name: ESC battery pads
parts.info: The battery leads land here: everything the quad uses comes in through these two pads.

parts.name: ESC plug
parts.info: The 8-pin cable to the flight controller: battery voltage, ground, current sensor, telemetry and the four motor signals.

parts.name: Capacitor 1000 µF 35 V
parts.info: Soldered across the battery pads. It soaks up the voltage spikes the ESC’s switching kicks back into the battery leads.

parts.name: Stack grommets
parts.info: Soft rubber between the boards: they keep motor vibration away from the gyro.

layers.info: Bottom board of the 30 × 30 stack: the four-in-one ESC.

layers.name: Camera
layers.info: The FPV camera, between two side plates at the front.

parts.name: FPV camera
parts.info: A 19 mm micro camera (approx.). It sends analog video down one wire; the pilot sees it about as fast as light, with no frame buffering.

parts.name: Camera side plates
parts.info: Carbon side plates; the camera is screwed between them at an upward tilt (not drawn).

parts.name: FC board
parts.info: The brain: it reads the gyro thousands of times a second, mixes in the pilot’s sticks and sends each motor a new speed.

parts.name: MCU STM32F405
parts.info: Runs Betaflight: the PID loop, the motor mixer, DShot out, CRSF in.

parts.name: Gyro ICM42688P
parts.info: Measures rotation on three axes, read by the MCU over SPI.

parts.name: OSD AT7456E
parts.info: Writes text (battery voltage, timer, warnings) over the camera picture before it goes to the VTX.

parts.name: Blackbox flash
parts.info: 16 MB log of every flight: gyro, sticks, motor outputs.

parts.name: BEC inductors
parts.info: Parts of the 5 V and 9 V converters that power the camera, receiver and VTX from the battery.

parts.name: USB-C
parts.info: For setting up Betaflight from a computer.

parts.name: FC plug
parts.info: The other end of the 8-pin cable from the ESC.

parts.name: FC pads
parts.info: Solder pads for the camera, VTX and receiver (layout approx.).

layers.name: VTX
layers.info: The video transmitter on top of the stack.

parts.name: VTX board
parts.info: Puts the camera picture (with the OSD on it) on a 5.8 GHz channel for the pilot’s goggles (approx.: a typical analog VTX).

parts.name: VTX shield
parts.info: Metal can over the RF amplifier.

parts.name: Top plate
parts.info: Top plate: the battery is strapped on it.

parts.name: Battery pad
parts.info: Grippy pad so the battery does not slide.

parts.name: VTX antenna
parts.info: Circularly polarised 5.8 GHz antenna (approx.).

parts.name: RX antenna
parts.info: 2.4 GHz dipole for the receiver (approx.).

parts.name: Battery 6S
parts.info: Six lithium-polymer cells in series. Everything on the quad runs from it; at full throttle it gives over 100 A.

parts.name: Battery XT60
parts.info: The battery’s XT60 plug (male pins inside the yellow body).

parts.name: XT60 (quad)
parts.info: The quad’s XT60 socket on its pigtail; unplug here to disarm completely.

parts.name: Balance lead
parts.info: Seven wires, one to each cell junction, used only by the charger to balance the cells.

layers.name: Props

parts.name: Props (CW)
parts.info: 5.1-inch tri-blade. Turning, it pushes air down; thrust grows roughly with the square of its speed.

parts.name: Props (CCW)
parts.info: 5.1-inch tri-blade. Turning, it pushes air down; thrust grows roughly with the square of its speed.

layers.info: Props on, from the top: 1 and 4 turn clockwise, 2 and 3 anticlockwise (props in).

wires.name: Battery lead +
wires.info: Red, 12 AWG. All the current for the quad leaves the battery here.

specs.Current: follows the throttle; over 100 A flat out

wires.name: Battery lead −
wires.info: Black, 12 AWG: the return path into the battery’s negative.

wires.name: Pigtail +
wires.info: Red 12 AWG from the XT60 socket to the ESC’s + pad.

wires.name: Pigtail −
wires.info: Black 12 AWG from the ESC’s − pad back to the XT60.

wires.name: Motor 1 phase A
wires.info: One of motor 1’s three wires (20 AWG, approx.). The ESC swings it between battery + and −, a third of a turn after the previous phase; the bell follows the turning field.

wires.name: FC battery voltage
wires.info: Battery voltage up to the FC, which makes its own 5 V and 9 V from it.

wires.name: Harness ground
wires.info: Ground shared by both boards.

wires.name: Current sensor
wires.info: An analog voltage from the ESC’s shunt amplifier: the FC turns it into amps and mAh used.

wires.name: DShot motor 1
wires.info: Digital throttle for one motor: a 16-bit frame (11-bit value, telemetry bit, checksum) at 600 kbit/s, sent every PID loop (thousands of times a second).

wires.name: DShot motor 2
wires.info: Digital throttle for one motor: a 16-bit frame (11-bit value, telemetry bit, checksum) at 600 kbit/s, sent every PID loop (thousands of times a second).

wires.name: Camera video
wires.info: Analog picture from the camera into the FC, where the OSD chip writes text over it.

wires.name: Camera 5 V
wires.info: 5 V from the FC’s regulator.

wires.name: Video to VTX
wires.info: The camera picture with the OSD text on it, on its way to the transmitter.

wires.name: VTX 9 V
wires.info: 9 V from the FC’s second regulator.

wires.name: SmartAudio
wires.info: One-wire serial: Betaflight sets the VTX channel and power through it (approx.).

wires.name: CRSF uplink
wires.info: Stick positions and switches from the pilot, in CRSF frames.

wires.name: CRSF telemetry
wires.info: Battery voltage and link quality back to the pilot’s radio.

wires.name: RX 5 V
wires.info: 5 V for the receiver.

wires.name: VTX coax
wires.info: Thin coax to the antenna: 5.8 GHz carrying the picture.

wires.name: RX antenna lead
wires.info: 2.4 GHz from the antenna into the receiver.
